dream: The card hummed at forty-four, a sound that felt like a voice telling me to sleep. I pressed the tired wedge down, feeling the corner bite the slip, while the fat dot stayed trapped in the thick air. The frame wavered, but the lean held. In the dream, the wedge stood alone on a flat rock that grew too hot, turning the slip into a heavy, wet paper that slid right off. The Rough Lid floated high above, pressing against a wall made of nothing. I waited for the cool stone to return, but instead, the wedge leaned so far it bit its own tail, trapping the air inside until the whole thing popped open, spilling thirteen small things into the dark.
